{{nihongo|'''Sumiyoshi Shrine'''|住吉神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in Sumiyoshi Higashifure, Ashibe-chō, {{ill|Iki, Nagasaki|Q861519|qid=Q861519}}, {{ill|Nagasaki Prefecture|Q169376|qid=Q169376}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}), its former rank under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} was {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=kokuhei chūsha}}, and it is now a {{ill|Beppyo shrine|Q10898274|qid=Q10898274}} of the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|Q908077|qid=Q908077}}. {{nihongo|'''Sumiyoshi Shrine'''|住吉神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Iki Island]].

== Enshrined deities ==
Sokotsutsu-no-o-no-Mikoto, Nakatsutsu-no-o-no-Mikoto, and Uwatsutsu-no-o-no-Mikoto are the main deities, collectively called the "{{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|Q1114013|qid=Q1114013|lt=Sumiyoshi Ōkami}}." {{ill|Ōkuninushi|abstract|Q276944|ca|Ōkuninushi|es|Ōkuninushi|fa|اوکونینوشی|fr|Ōkuninushi|hu|Ókuninusi|id|Ookuninushi|it|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主|ko|오오쿠니누시|mni|ꯑꯣꯀꯨꯅꯤꯅꯨꯁꯤ|pl|Ōkuninushi|pt|Ookuninushi|ru|Окунинуси|simple|Ōkuninushi|sr|Okuninuši|sv|Ōkuninushi|tr|Ōkuninushi|uk|Окунінуші|vi|Ōkuninushi|zh|大國主|qid=Q276944|lt=Yachihoko-no-Kami}} is enshrined in the associated hall.

== History ==
According to shrine tradition, {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}}, who accomplished {{ill|Three Han Campaign|Q11249435|qid=Q11249435}} under the protection of the Sumiyoshi deities, landed on her return at present Ōura-fure, Gōnoura-chō, Iki City and enshrined the three deities there (hence the claim of being "Japan's first Sumiyoshi Shrine"). It later moved to the current location by {{ill|Oracle|Q217123|qid=Q217123}}. In the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}' it was ranked as myōjin taisha. It also claims to be the leading shrine in Nagasaki Prefecture.

In May {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 4 ({{ill|1871|Q7746|qid=Q7746}}), it was ranked kokuhei chūsha.

== Annual festival ==
* Grand annual festival - November 9

== Cultural properties ==
== Nagasaki Prefecture designated cultural property ==
* Tangible cultural property
** Silk painting of the Four Kōya Shrine Deities (painting) - made after the middle Muromachi period. Donated in Meiji 27 (1894) by a donor from Ashibe-chō living in Osaka. Designated March 4, Shōwa 50 (1975)<ref name="説明板"/><ref>'Cultural Properties of Iki City,' Iki City Board of Education, Nagasaki, 2017, p.20.</ref>.

== Iki City designated cultural properties ==
* Tangible cultural properties
** 17 sacred mirrors of Sumiyoshi Shrine (crafts) - mirrors found in 1871 in the sacred pond within Sumiyoshi Shrine precincts. Breakdown: 12 continental-style mirrors, 5 Japanese-style mirrors. Designated January 1, Shōwa 51 (1976)<ref name="説明板">Precinct information board.</ref><ref>'Cultural Properties of Iki City,' Iki City Board of Education, Nagasaki, 2017, p.90.</ref>.
** Miyuki-bune (craft) - boat used in the boat ritual of the Sumiyoshi Shrine annual festival. Newly built in Shōwa 8 (1933)<ref>'Cultural Properties of Iki City,' Iki City Board of Education, Nagasaki, 2017, p.98.</ref>.
* Natural monument
** [[ファイル:Iki sumiyoshi shrine sando.jpg|サムネイル|Haiden viewed from approach]][[ファイル:Iki sumiyoshishrine kusu.jpg|サムネイル|"Married camphor trees" in front of haiden]]Two camphor trees of Sumiyoshi Shrine - designated January 1, Shōwa 51 (1976)<ref name="説明板"/><ref>'Cultural Properties of Iki City,' Iki City Board of Education, Nagasaki, 2017, p.196.</ref>.
